speaker: Doctor
text:
The blood work and X-ray are normal, which makes infectious causes like tuberculosis or acute gout unlikely. Given your family history, does the swelling come and go, and is there a history of these episodes occurring in other joints or your eyes?

speaker: Doctor
text: I'm glad the inflammatory markers and X-ray are normal; this points away from infection or acute crystal arthropathy. To distinguish between conditions like familial Mediterranean fever, gout without acute inflammation, or a mechanical issue, have you noticed that the swelling resolves completely on its own between episodes? Also, do you have any history of abdominal pain or rash during these flare-ups?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.
